text_blocks.snippet: Central Illinois residents are currently targeted by several active, prominent scams, including AI voice-cloning phone schemes, spoofed law enforcement calls, and gift card or tampering traps.

list.snippet: AI Voice-Cloning & Family Emergency Scams: Scammers use artificial intelligence to mimic the voices of loved ones or children, claiming they are in an urgent accident, hospital, or legal emergency and demanding immediate payment via Zelle, Cash App, wire transfer, or cryptocurrency .

Spoofed Sheriff/Police & Warrant Scams: Scammers spoof local sheriff or police numbers (such as in Williamson County) or federal/U.S. Attorney numbers, posing as detectives or officers and claiming the victim has a missed court date or active arrest warrant. They demand immediate cash bonds or payment over the phone.

Fake Traffic & Toll Violation Texts: Fraudulent text messages mimicking the Illinois Tollway, Secretary of State, or local traffic courts claim you owe unpaid fines and threaten driver's license suspension unless you click a link and pay. (Note: State agencies do not demand or request fine payments via unprompted text) .

Gift Card & Retail Tampering: Criminals tamper with gift cards on open store racks by peeling off security covers, photographing PINs, and reapplying stickers, or scraping middle codes to drain funds the moment a card is activated.

Storm Chaser & Contractor Scams: Following spring and summer storms, dishonest contractors and fake public adjusters move through Central Illinois neighborhoods, offering "free inspections" and pressuring homeowners into large upfront cash payments for unnecessary or unfinished repairs.

High-Dollar Gold Bar & Investment Fraud: Scammers build long-term online or phone trust with seniors or investors, convincing them to liquidate retirement accounts or buy physical gold bars to hand over to "couriers" for safekeeping.
Verify independently: Hang up and call official numbers directly (never use the phone number provided in a suspicious text or caller ID).
Check official hotlines: You can report suspected fraud or get assistance from the Office of the Illinois Attorney General using their Springfield Consumer Fraud Hotline at 1-800-243-0618.

list.snippet: Never pay via gift card or crypto: Legitimate government agencies, police departments, and utilities will never demand payment in gift cards, prepaid debit cards, wire transfers, or cryptocurrency.
Inspect gift cards: If you buy gift cards, check the back for peeled stickers or missing scratch-off panels, or ask for cards kept securely behind the counter.

text_blocks.snippet: If you or someone you know received a specific message or call, let me know what they claimed (e.g., a fake warrant, a tech support alert, or an online listing) and I can give you exact steps to verify it.
